description:
Found by the cold review of fz-5xp.31.

`dispatch_shapes!` in src/ir_interp/extern_call.rs enumerates 31 argument shapes
-- each arity up to MAX_INTERP_EXTERN_ARGS, times each assignment of its
parameters to the integer and float register banks. `behavior/extern_float_lanes`
exercises five of them. Arity 0, all eight arity-3 shapes and all sixteen
arity-4 shapes have no test at all.

An arm naming the wrong bank for a position is a SILENT WRONG ANSWER, not a
crash, which is precisely how the original defect behaved (`libc::sqrt(9.0)`
returned 9.0).

The review found a cheap way to reach any shape exactly: both SysV and AAPCS64
ignore argument registers the callee never reads, so a real libc function can be
declared with extra trailing parameters to select an arm while keeping an exact
expected value -- e.g. `extern "C" fn libc::ldexp(float, integer, float, integer)`
reaches shape (4, 0b0101). It verified all 30 arity-1..4 arms this way, 90/90
correct across the three doors; the coverage that is missing is the STANDING
kind, not a one-off.

DONE = a fixture (or generated family) covering every shape on all three doors,
so a future edit to the table cannot transpose two arms unnoticed.

WATCH OUT: relies on the argument-register-ignoring property above. State it in
the fixture, since a reader will otherwise think the declarations are wrong.
title: Only 5 of 31 extern argument shapes are exercised
